WHEREAS, Art. IX, § II, { I[(a)(6) of the Georgia Constitution of 1983 authorizes the Town of Clermont, Georgia to regulate sewage collection and disposal systems; and

WHEREAS, the Town of Clermont, Georgia has no public operated treatment works, and therefore new development within the Town of Clermont, Georgia must depend upon septic tank systems and/or privately owned private or public sewer facilities; and

WHEREAS, the Town Council of the Town of Clermont, Georgia, has determined that it is in the best interest in the health, safety and welfare of the citizens and residents of the Town of Clermont, Georgia that the Town of Clermont have sewer regulations as provided by this ordinance; and

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED by the above-referenced authority, and the authority of Town Charter of the Town of Clermont, Georgia, and it is so ordained as follows:

I. GENERAL SEWER USE REQUIREMENTS 1.1.1. Use of public sewers required.

(A) It shall be unlawful to discharge to any natural outlet within the Town, or in any area under the jurisdiction of the Town, any sewage or other polluted waters, except where suitable treatment has been provided in accordance with subsequent provision of this ordinance.

(B) Except as hereinafter provided, it shall be unlawful to construct any privy, privy vault, septic tank, cesspool, or other facility intended or used for the disposal of sewage, if there is a public sewer within three hundred (300) feet of the subject property.

(C) The owner of all houses, buildings or property used for human occupancy, employment, recreation or other purposes, situated within the Town and abutting on any street, alley or rightof-way in which there is not located nor may in the future be located a public sanitary or combined sewer of the Town, is hereby required at his expense to install suitable toilet facilities therein, and to connect such facilities directly with the proper public sewer in accordance with the provision of this Ordinance, within ninety (90) days after the date of official notice to do so, provided that there is a public sewer within three hundred (300) feet of the property line.

1.1.2. Private sewage disposal.

(A) Definitions. As used in this Section, private facility means a sewage treatment facility providing sewage disposal to property owned only by a single owner. Examples would include a facility serving a single industrial site, or a facility serving a mobile home park where all lots are owned by a single owner. Public facility means a sewage treatment facility providing sewage disposal to more than one property owned by different owners. Examples would include a facility serving an industrial park with several owners, or a facility serving a subdivision with separate homeowners.

(B) Private Facilities. Privately-owned private facilities are permitted, subject to approval by the Town Council of the Town of Clermont, Georgia or its designated agent. All proposed private facilities that require permitting under the Federal Clean Water Act shall require approval by the Town Council of the Town of Clermont prior to submission of permit application.

(C) Public Facilities. Public facilities that are privately owned are permitted, subject to approval by the Town Council of the Town of Clermont, Georgia or its designated agent. Sewage treatment facilities that serve more than one property owner shall be allowed subject to the requirements of this ordinance.

(D) Before commencement of construction of a privately-owned private facility or privatelyowned public facility, the owner shall first obtain a written permit from the State Department of Human Resources (DHR), Division of Public Health or from the State Environmental Protection Division (EPD), as applicable. The Town Council or its designated agent can approve such facilities, subject to the facilities receiving its written State permit.

(E) The type, capacities, location and layout of private facilities shall comply with all recommendations of the DHR or EPD.

(F) The owner shall operate and maintain the private facilities in a sanitary manner, as determined by the state and Town’s designated agents at no expense to the Town.

(G) No statement contained in this article shall be construed to interfere with any additional requirements that may be imposed by state and Town’s designated agents.

(H) The owner of a failed private facility or private sewer system must connect to a public sewer within sixty (60) days of failure provided there is a public service within three hundred (300) feet of the property line and must abandon the private system, and ensure no improper disposal or leakage of waste.

Il. RESIDENTIAL LOT WASTE TREATMENT PROVISIONS 1.2.1. Purpose

It is the purpose of Section II to regulate the available types of waste treatment options for individual uses in the Town. The Town has experience with individual septic systems and traditional gravity flow systems, and such systems are appropriate for the Town. Under more limited circumstances, private sewage facilities may be permitted. Town recognizes that the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency has found low pressure sewer systems to have increased energy demands, higher maintenance requirements, and higher costs to the homeowner. The Town has further determined that the ongoing maintenance issues created by such systems lead to greater future problems than in a conventional gravity flow sewer system. Such systems have many more mechanical and powered parts and are therefore subject to much higher failure rates. Preventative maintenance requirements are higher, and power outages can result in overflows and damage to residences. Life cycle replacement costs are higher than gravity sewers. Therefore, this Section is adopted to regulate such systems, in the interest of protecting the health, safety and welfare of the citizens of Town.

1.2.2. Definitions

As used in this ordinance, words shall have their common meaning and significance, except for the specifically defined terms below:

Effluent: The flow of liquids and solids from a structure's sewage plumbing system; e.g., human waste, waste water, etc.

Low Pressure Sewer System: A sewer system that uses pressure to move the effluent from individual lots to the main sewer lines. Pressure sewers typically break down large solids in a

pumping station located on an individual lot before they are transported through the collection system (sewer mains) to the treatment facility. Such systems include grinder pump systems and septic tank effluent pump systems. Systems which use a pump to pump waste from a septic tank to a septic field on the same lot are not included in this definition.

Low Pressure Sewer System Cluster: A pressure sewer system with a common low pressure line that connects several residences by individual pumps to a central or common pump station.

Private (sewage) facility means a privately-owned sewage treatment facility providing sewage disposal to property owned only by a single owner, but does not include septic tank systems serving only one residential lot, or one commercial lot that generates on average the same amount of daily sewage as one residential lot. Examples would include a facility serving a single industrial site, or a facility serving a mobile home park where all lots are owned by a single owner.

Public (sewage) facility means a privately owned sewage treatment facility providing sewage disposal to more than one property owned by different owners. Examples would include a facility serving an industrial park with several owners, or a facility serving a subdivision with separate homeowners.

1.2.3. Regulation of Waste Treatment Facilities

A. Low pressure sewer systems (including low pressure sewer system clusters) are prohibited in the Town of Clermont. Individual residential lots may either contain individual onsite sewage management systems (i.e., septic systems) approved by the Hall County Board of Health, or may be connected to a public gravity flow sewer system. Private sewage facilities and public sewage facilities are regulated by this ordinance.

B. Sewage treatment and handling systems for individual residential lots not otherwise covered or defined specifically by this ordinance, or as may be invented in the future, shall only be permitted upon approval of the Town Council or its designated agent. The applicant shall submit an application as required by the Town Council or its designated agent, containing plans, specifications and other information considered pertinent in the judgment of the Town Council or its designated agent. The Town Council or its designated agent shall not permit systems or technologies that are unproven, that increase the risks of environmental contamination, that do not meet the standards contained in this ordinance or other applicable ordinance, that increase costs or burdens on the Town's sewer system or to individual property owners, or that are found to be a threat in any way to the health, safety or welfare of the citizens of the Town.

1.2.4. Interpretation

It shall be the duty of the Town Council or its designated agent to classify proposed systems. If there is a question as to the type of system proposed, or whether it is permitted or prohibited, the Town Council or its designated agent shall make the final interpretation for the water department. An agent’s determination may be appealed to the Town Council.

When requested by the Town Council or its designated agent, a user must submit information on the nature and characteristics of its wastewater within thirty (30) days of request. The Town Council or its designated agent is authorized to prepare a form for this purpose and may periodically require users to update this information.

1.3.2. Privately owned private or public facilities permit requirement.

(A) No privately owned private or public facilities shall operate without first obtaining a permit from the Town Council or its designated agent.

(B) Any violation of the terms and conditions of a permit shall be deemed a violation of this Ordinance and subjects the permittee to the sanctions set out in 1.7.6 through 1.8.4 of this Ordinance. Obtaining a permit does not relieve a permittee of its obligation to comply with all federal and state pretreatment standards or requirements or with any other requirements of federal, state and local law.

1.3.3. New privately owned private or public facilities. Any operator required to obtain a permit who proposes to begin operations must obtain such permit prior to the beginning operations. An application for this privately owned private or public facilities permit must be submitted prior to the date upon which operations will begin.

1.3.4. Same--Application contents.

(A) All operators required to obtain a privately owned private or public facilities permit must submit a permit application. The Town Council or its designated agent may require all operators to submit as part of an application the following information:

- (1) All information required by 1.5.1 of this Ordinance.

- (2) Description of activities, facilities and plant processes on the premises, including a list of all raw materials and chemicals used or stored at the facility;

- (3) | Number and type of employees, hours of operation, and proposed or actual hours of operation;

- (4) Site plans, floor plans, mechanical and plumbing plans, and details to show all sewers, floor drains, and appurtenances by size, location, and elevation, and all points of discharge;

- (5) Time and duration of discharges; and

- (6) All plans, designs, engineering sheets and other information that indicates that the sewer facility meets the standard specifications for sewer mains and sewer infrastructure as set out within Appendix 1.

- (7) Any other information as may be deemed necessary by the Town Council or its designated agent to evaluate the privately owned private or public facilities permit application.

(B) Incomplete or inaccurate applications will not be processed and will be returned to the applicant for revision.

(C) The permit application should be completed and returned thirty (30) days from the receipt of the permit application.

1.3.5. Application signatories and certification.

All privately owned private or public facility permit applications and operator reports must be signed by an authorized representative of the operator and contain the following certification statement:

"I certify under penalty of law this document and all attachments were prepared under my direction or supervision in accordance with a system designed to assure that qualified personnel properly gather and evaluate any information submitted. Based on my inquiry of the person or persons who manage the system, or those persons directly responsible for gathering the information, the information submitted is, to the best of my knowledge and belief, true, accurate, and complete. I am aware that there are significant penalties for submitting false information, including the possibility of fine and imprisonment for knowing violations."

1.5.8. Analytical requirements.

All pollutant analyses, including sampling techniques, to be submitted as part of a privately owned private or public facility permit application or report shall be performed in accordance with the techniques prescribed in 40 CFR Part 136, unless otherwise specified in an applicable categorical treatment standard. If 40 CFR Part 136 does not contain sampling or analytical techniques for the pollutant in question, sampling and analyses must be performed in accordance with procedures approved by EPA.

1.5.9, Sample collection.

(A) Except as indicated in subsection (b) below, the operator must collect wastewater samples using flow proportional composite collection techniques. In the event flow proportional sampling is infeasible, the Town Council or its designated agent may authorize the use of time proportional sampling or minimum of four (4) grab samples where the operator demonstrates that this will provide a representative sample of the effluent being discharged. In addition, grab samples may be required to show compliance with instantaneous discharge limits.

(B) Samples for oil and grease, temperature, pH, cyanide, phenols, sulfides and volatile organic compounds must be obtained using grab collection techniques.

1.5.10. Timing.

Written reports will be deemed to have been submitted on the date postmarked. For reports which are not mailed, postage prepaid, into a mail facility serviced by the United States Postal Service, the date of receipt of the report shall govern.

1.5.11 Record keeping.

Users subject to the reporting requirements of this Ordinance shall retain, and make available for inspection and copying, all records of information obtained pursuant to any monitoring activities required by this Ordinance and any additional records of information obtained pursuant to monitoring activities undertaken by the operator independent of such requirements. Records shall include the date, exact place, method and time of sampling, and the name of the person(s) taking the samples, the dates the analyses were performed, who performed the analyses; the analytical techniques or methods used; and the results of such analyses. These records shall remain available for a period of at least three (3) years. This period shall be automatically extended for the duration of any litigation concerning the operator, or where the user has been specifically notified of a longer retention period by the Town Council or its designated agent.

VI. COMPLIANCE MONITORING 1.6.1. Inspection, Entry of Premises.

The Town Council or its designated agent, or other authorized representatives of state and federal regulatory agencies, shall have the right to enter the premises of any operator to determine whether the operator is complying with all requirements of this Ordinance and any privately owned private or public facility permit or order issued hereunder. Operators shall allow the Town Council or its designated agent ready access to all parts of the premises for the purposes of inspection, sampling, records examination and copying, and the performance of any additional duties. The Town Council or its designated agent shall also have the right to enter all private properties through which the Town holds a utility easement for the purposes of, but not limited to, inspection, observation, measurement, sampling, repair and maintenance of any portion of the wastewater facilities lying within such easement. All entry and subsequent work on such easement shall be done in full accord with the terms of the utility easement pertaining to such property.

- (1) Where an operator has security measures in force which require proper identification and clearance before entry into its premises, the operator shall make necessary arrangements with its security guards so that, upon presentation of suitable identification, the Town Council or its designated agent will be permitted to enter without delay for the purposes of performing specific responsibilities.

- (2) The Town Council or its designated agent shall have the right to set up on the operator’s property, or require installation of, such devices as are necessary to conduct sampling and/or metering of the operator's operations.

- (3) The Town Council or its designated agent may require the operator to install monitoring equipment as necessary. The facility's sampling and monitoring equipment shall be

20

maintained at all times in a safe and proper operating condition by the operator at its own expense. All devices used to measure wastewater flow and quality shall be calibrated as needed to ensure accuracy.

- (4) Any temporary or permanent obstruction to safe and easy access to the facility to be inspected and/or sampled shall be promptly removed by the operator at the written or verbal request of the Town Council or its designated agent and shall not be replaced. The costs of clearing such access shall be borne by the operator.

- (5) Unreasonable delays in allowing the Town Council or its designated agent access to the operator's premises shall be a violation of this Ordinance.

1.6.2. Search warrants.
19:
If the Town Council or its designated agent has been refused access to a building, structure, or property, or any part thereof, and is able to demonstrate probable cause to believe that there may be a violation of this Ordinance, or that there is need to inspect and/or sample as part of a routine inspection and sampling program of the Town designed to verify compliance with this Ordinance or any permit or order issued hereunder, or to protect the overall public health, safety and welfare of the community, then the Town Council or its desi gnated agent may seek issuance of a search warrant from the magistrate or superior courts of Hall County.

Vl. _ADMINISTRATIVE ENFORCEMENT REMEDIES

1.7.1. Notification of violation.

When the Town Council or its designated agent finds that an operator has violated, or continues to violate, any provision of this Ordinance, a privately owned private or public facility permit or order issued hereunder, or any other treatment standard or requirement, the Town Council or its designated agent may serve upon that user a written notice of violation. Within seven (7) days of the receipt of this notice, an explanation of the violation and a plan for the satisfactory correction and prevention thereof to include specific required actions shall be submitted by the operator to the Town Council or its designated agent. Submission of this plan in no way relieves the operator of liability for any violations occurring before or after receipt of the notice of violation. Nothing in this section shall limit the authority of the Town Council or its designated agent to take any action, including emergency actions or any other enforcement action, without first issuing a notice of violation.

1.7.2. Consent orders.

The Town may enter into consent orders, assurances of voluntary compliance, or other similar documents establishing an agreement with any operator responsible for noncompliance. Such documents will include specific action to be taken by the operator to correct the noncompliance with a time period specified by the document. Such documents shall have the force and effect as the administrative orders issued pursuant to this Ordinance and shall be judicially enforceable.

21

1.7.3. Show cause hearing.

The privately owned private or public facility may order an operator which has violated, or continues to violate, any provision of this Ordinance, a privately owned private or public facility permit or order issued hereunder, or any other treatment standard or requirement, to appear before the Town Council or its designated agent and show cause why the proposed enforcement action should not be taken. If the Town Council or its designated agent chooses to have such a hearing, notice shall be served on the user specifying the time and place for the meeting, the proposed enforcement action, the reasons for such action, and a request that the user show cause why the proposed enforcement action should not be taken. The notice of the meeting shall be served personally or by registered or certified mail (return receipt requested) at least thirty (30) days prior to the hearing. Such notice may be served on any authorized representative of the user. A show cause hearing shall not be a bar against, or prerequisite for, taking any other action against the operator.

1.7.4. Compliance orders.

When the Town Council or its designated agent finds that an operator has violated, or continues to violate, any provision of this Ordinance, a wastewater discharge permit or order issued hereunder, or any other treatment standard or requirement, the Town Council or its designated agent may issue an order to the operator responsible for the discharge directing that the operator come into compliance within a specified time. If the user does not come into compliance within the time provided, sewer service may be discontinued unless adequate treatment facilities, device or other related appurtenances are installed and properly operated. Compliance orders also may contain other requirements to address noncompliance, including additional self-monitoring and management practices designed to minimize the amount of pollutants discharged to the sewer. A compliance order may not extend the deadline for compliance established or pretreatment standard or requirement, not does a compliance order relieve the operator of liability for any violation, including any continuing violation. Issuance of a compliance order shall not be a bar against, or a prerequisite for, taking any other action against the operator.

1.7.5. Cease and desist orders.

(A) | When the Town Council or its designated agent finds that a operator has violated, or continues to violate, any provision of this Ordinance, a privately owned private or public facility permit or order issued hereunder, or any other treatment standard or requirement, or that the user's past violations are likely to recur, the Town Council or its designated agent may issue an order to the operator directing it to cease and desist all such violations and directing the operator to:

- (1) Immediately comply with all requirements; and (2) Take such appropriate remedial or preventive action as may be needed to properly address a continuing or threatened violation, including halting operations and/or terminating the discharge.

22

(B) Issuance of a cease and desist order shall not be a bar against, or prerequisite for, taking any other action against the operator.

1.7.6. Administrative fines.
20:
(A) When the Town Council or its designated agent finds that an operator has violated, or continues to violate, any provision of this Ordinance, a privately owned private or public facility permit or order issued hereunder, or any other treatment standard or requirement, the Town Council or its designated agent may fine such operator in an amount not to exceed one thousand dollars ($1,000.00), per day. Such fines shall be assessed on a per-violation, per-day basis. In the case of monthly or other long-term average discharge limits, fines shall be assessed for each day during the period of violation.

(B) Unpaid charges, fines and penalties shall, after fifteen (15) calendar days, be assessed an additional penalty of fifteen (15) percent of the unpaid balance, and interest shall accrue thereafter at a rate of one and one-half (1 1/2) percent per month. A lien against the operator's property will be sought for unpaid charges, fines and penalties.

(C) Operators desiring to dispute such fines must file a written request for the Town Council or its designated agent to reconsider the fine along with full payment of the fine amount within thirty (30) days of being notified of the fine. Where a request has merit, the Town Council or its designated agent may convene a hearing on the matter. In the event the user's appeal is successful, the payment, together with any interest accruing thereto, shall be returned to the operator. The Town Council or its designated agent may add the costs of preparing administrative enforcement actions, such as notices and orders, to the fine.

(D) Issuance of an administrative fine shall not be a bar against or a prerequisite for taking any other action against the operator.

1.7.7. Emergency suspensions.

(A) The Town Council or its designated agent may immediately suspend an operator's discharge, after informal notice to operator, whenever such suspension is necessary to stop an actual or threatened discharge which reasonably appears to present or cause an imminent or substantial endangerment to the health or welfare of persons. The Town Council or its designated agent may also immediately suspend an operator's discharge, after notice and opportunity to respond, that threatens to interfere with the operation of the privately owned private or public facility or which presents, or may present, an endangerment to the environment.

- (1) Any operator notified of a suspension of its discharge shall immediately stop or eliminate its contribution. In the event of an operator's failure to immediately comply voluntarily with the suspension order, the Town Council or its designated agent may take such steps as deemed necessary, including immediate severance of the sewer connection, to prevent or minimize damage to the privately owned private or public facility, its receiving stream, or endangerment to any individuals. The Town Council or its designated agent may allow the user

23

to recommence its discharge when the operator has demonstrated to the satisfaction of the Town Council or its designated agent that the period of endangerment has passed, unless the termination proceedings under 1.7.8 are initiated against the operators.

- (2) An operator that is responsible, in whole or in part, for any discharge presenting imminent endangerment shall submit a detailed written statement describing the causes of the harmful contribution and the measures taken to prevent any future occurrences to the Town Council or its designated agent prior to the date of any show cause or termination hearing under this Ordinance.

(B) Nothing in this section shall be interpreted as requiring a hearing prior to any emergency suspension under this section.

1.7.8. Termination of permit.

(A) In addition to the provisions in 1.7.6 of this Ordinance, any operator who violates the following conditions is subject to permit termination:

- (1) Violation of privately owned private or public facility permit conditions;

- (2) Failure to accurately report the wastewater constituents and characteristics of its discharge;

- (3) Failure to report significant changes in operations or wastewater volume, constituents and characteristics prior to discharge;

- (4) Refusal of reasonable access to the operator's premises for the purpose of inspection, monitoring or sampling; or

- (5) Violation of the treatment standards in this Ordinance.

(B) Such operator will be notified of the proposed termination of its discharge and be offered an opportunity to show cause under 1.7.3 of this Ordinance why the proposed action should not be taken. Exercise of this option by the Town Council or its designated agent shall not be a bar to, or prerequisite for, taking any other action against the operator.

VIL. JUDICIAL ENFORCEMENT REMEDIES 1.8.1. Injunctive relief.

When the Town Council or its designated agent finds that an operator has violated, or continues to violate, any provision of this Ordinance, a privately owned private or public facility permit, or order issued hereunder, or any other treatment standard or requirement, the Town Council or its designated agent may petition the superior court through the Town's attorney for the issuance of temporary or permanent injunction, as appropriate. Said temporary or permanent injunction shall restrain or compel the specific performance of the wastewater discharge permit, order or other requirement for the user to conduct environmental remediation. The Town

24

Council or its designated agent may also seek restitution, costs of environmental remediation, and attorney's fees for bringing the action. A petition for injunctive relief shall not be a bar against, or a prerequisite for, taking any other action against an operator.

1.8.2. Civil penalties.
21:
(A) An operator who has violated, or continues to violate, any provision of this Ordinance, a wastewater discharge permit, or order issued hereunder, or any other pretreatment standard or requirement shall be liable to the Town for a maximum civil penalty of one thousand dollars ($1,000.00) per violation per day. In the case of monthly or other long-term average discharge limit, penalties shall accrue for each day during the period of the violation.

(B) The Town Council or its designated agent may recover reasonable attorney's fees, court costs, and other expenses associated with enforcement activities, including sampling and monitoring expenses, the cost of remediation measures and clean-up, and the cost of any actual damages incurred by the Town.

(C) In determining the amount of civil liability, the court shall take into account all relevant circumstances including, but not limited to, the extent of harm caused by the violation, the magnitude and duration of the violation, any economic benefit gained through the operator's violation, corrective actions by the user, the compliance history of the operator, and any other factor as justice requires.

(D) Filing a suit for civil penalties shall not be a bar against, or a prerequisite for, taking any other action against an operator.

(E) All violations of this Ordinance may be prosecuted in the municipal or superior courts. 1.8.3. Criminal prosecution.

(A) An operator who willfully or negligently violates any provision of this Ordinance, a privately owned private or public facility permit, or order issued hereunder, or any other treatment standard or requirement shall, upon conviction, be guilty of a misdemeanor punishable by a fine of not more than one thousand dollars ($1,000.00) per violation per day, or imprisonment for not more than six (6) months per violation per day, or both.

(B) An operator who willfully or negli gently introduces any substance into privately owned private or public facility which causes personal injury or property damage shall, upon conviction, be guilty of a misdemeanor and be subject to a penalty of at least one thousand dollars ($1,000.00), or be subject to imprisonment for not more than six (6) months, or both. This penalty shall be in addition to any other cause of action for personal injury or property damage available under state law.

(C) Anoperator who knowingly makes any false statements, representations or certifications in any application, record, report, plan or other documentation filed, or required to be maintained, pursuant to this Ordinance, wastewater discharge permit, or order issued hereunder, or who falsifies, tampers with, or knowingly renders inaccurate any monitoring

25

device or method required under this Ordinance shall, upon conviction, be punished by a fine of not more than five hundred dollars ($500.00) per violation per day, or imprisonment for not more than six (6) months, or both.

(D) Inthe event of a second conviction, an operator shall be punished by a fine of not more than one thousand dollars ($1,000.00) per violation per day, or imprisonment for not more than six (6) months, or both.

(E) All violations of this Ordinance may be prosecuted in the municipal or superior courts.

1.8.4. Remedies nonexclusive.

The remedies provided for in this Ordinance are not exclusive. The Town Council or its designated agent may take any, all, or any combination of these actions against a noncompliant operator. Enforcement of pretreatment violations will generally be in accordance with the Town's enforcement response plan. However, the Town Council or its designated agent may take other action against any operator when the circumstances warrant; further, the Town Council or its designated agent is empowered to take more than one (1) enforcement action against any noncompliant operator.
